"Paul, a servant of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ, for the faith of the chosen people of God and knowledge of the truth that agrees with godliness, "
"with the certain hope of eternal life that the non-lying God promised before all the ages of time. "
"But at the right time, he revealed his word by the proclamation, the one I was entrusted with by the command of God our Savior. "
<textarea data-i="field" dir="ltr" placeholder="What is this section saying? Who is speaking, to whom, and what will be hard to render?" rows="3" style=@b165b1e79d79 .value="">
"To Titus, a true son in a common faith. Grace and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Savior. "
"For this purpose I left you in Crete, that you might set in order the things not yet being complete and ordain elders in every city as I directed you— "
<textarea data-i="field" dir="ltr" placeholder="What is this section saying? Who is speaking, to whom, and what will be hard to render?" rows="3" style=@b165b1e79d79 .value="">
"if anyone is blameless, a husband of one wife, having faithful children not accused of reckless behavior or rebellion. "
"For the overseer must be blameless, as a household manager of God, not arrogant, not easily angered, not addicted to wine, not a brawler, not greedy. "
<textarea data-i="field" dir="ltr" placeholder="What is this section saying? Who is speaking, to whom, and what will be hard to render?" rows="3" style=@b165b1e79d79 .value="">
"Instead, he must be hospitable, a friend of what is good, sensible, righteous, holy, self-controlled. "
"He must hold tightly to the trustworthy message that is in accordance with the teaching, so that he may be able both to encourage others with sound teaching and to rebuke the ones opposing {him}. "
<textarea data-i="field" dir="ltr" placeholder="What is this section saying? Who is speaking, to whom, and what will be hard to render?" rows="3" style=@b165b1e79d79 .value="">
"For there are many rebellious people, empty talkers and deceivers, especially the ones from the circumcision. "
"It is necessary to stop them. They are upsetting whole households, teaching what they should not for the sake of shameful profit. "
<textarea data-i="field" dir="ltr" placeholder="What is this section saying? Who is speaking, to whom, and what will be hard to render?" rows="3" style=@b165b1e79d79 .value="">
"One of them, of their own prophets, has said, “Cretans {are} always liars, evil beasts, lazy bellies.” "
"This testimony is true. For this reason, rebuke them severely, so that they may be sound in the faith, "
"not paying any attention to Jewish myths or to commands of people turning away from the truth. "
<textarea data-i="field" dir="ltr" placeholder="What is this section saying? Who is speaking, to whom, and what will be hard to render?" rows="3" style=@b165b1e79d79 .value="">
"All things {are} pure to the ones {who are} pure. But to the ones having been corrupted and unbelieving, nothing {is} pure, but both their minds and consciences have been corrupted. "
"They profess to know God, but they deny {him} by their actions, being detestable and disobedient and unfit for any good work. "
<textarea data-i="field" dir="ltr" placeholder="What is this section saying? Who is speaking, to whom, and what will be hard to render?" rows="3" style=@b165b1e79d79 .value="">

<div data-frame="intro" data-i="choice" data-testid="helps-note" data-tone="accent" dir="ltr" role="button" tabindex="0" style=@3341312e2dcc>
"Paul formally introduces this letter in verses 1–4. Writers often began letters in this way in the ancient Near East."
"In verses 6–9, Paul lists several qualities that a man must have if he is to be an elder in the church. (See: rc://*/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns) Paul gives a similar list in 1 Timothy 3."
<div data-frame="1" data-i="choice" data-testid="helps-note" data-tone="accent" dir="ltr" role="button" tabindex="0" style=@3341312e2dcc>
"“for the faith of the chosen people of God and knowledge of the truth”"

" are abstract nouns. If it would be more clear in your language, you could express those ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [to help God’s chosen people to continue to trust him and to know every true thing]"
<div data-frame="1" data-i="choice" data-testid="helps-note" data-tone="accent" dir="ltr" role="button" tabindex="0" style=@3341312e2dcc>

"If your language does not use this passive form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [of the people whom God has chosen]"
<div data-frame="1" data-i="choice" data-testid="helps-note" data-tone="accent" dir="ltr" role="button" tabindex="0" style=@3341312e2dcc>

"Paul is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You could supply these words from earlier in the sentence if it would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and for their knowledge of the truth] or [and so that the chosen people of God might know the truth]"
<div data-frame="1" data-i="choice" data-testid="helps-note" data-tone="accent" dir="ltr" role="button" tabindex="0" style=@3341312e2dcc>
" is an abstract noun that refers to living in a way that pleases God. Alternate translation: [that is suitable for honoring God]"
<div data-frame="2" data-i="choice" data-testid="helps-note" data-tone="accent" dir="ltr" role="button" tabindex="0" style=@3341312e2dcc>
"“with the certain hope of eternal life”"
", meaning that if we live to please God, we will have hope of eternal life. Alternate translation: [which gives us the certain hope of everlasting life] or (2) "
", meaning that this hope of eternal life is part of the truth, and that knowing the truth gives hope of eternal life. Alternate translation: [and that teaches us to expect…"
<div data-frame="2" data-i="choice" data-testid="helps-note" data-tone="accent" dir="ltr" role="button" tabindex="0" style=@3341312e2dcc>
"“with the certain hope of eternal life”"
"If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of "
", you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [which leads us to confidently expect eternal life]"
<div data-frame="2" data-i="choice" data-testid="helps-note" data-tone="accent" dir="ltr" role="button" tabindex="0" style=@3341312e2dcc>
"If it would be clearer in your language, you could use a positive expression here instead of this double negative. Alternate translation: [the God who is completely trustworthy]"
<div data-frame="2" data-i="choice" data-testid="helps-note" data-tone="accent" dir="ltr" role="button" tabindex="0" style=@3341312e2dcc>
<div data-frame="3" data-i="choice" data-testid="helps-note" data-tone="accent" dir="ltr" role="button" tabindex="0" style=@3341312e2dcc>
<div data-frame="3" data-i="choice" data-testid="helps-note" data-tone="accent" dir="ltr" role="button" tabindex="0" style=@3341312e2dcc>
"Paul speaks of God’s word as if it were an object that could be visibly shown to people. Alternate translation: [he caused me to understand his message]"
<div data-frame="3" data-i="choice" data-testid="helps-note" data-tone="accent" dir="ltr" role="button" tabindex="0" style=@3341312e2dcc>
"Paul assumes that his readers will understand that "

" refers to the message of the gospel of Jesus Christ. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [by means of the proclamation of the message about Jesus]"
<div data-frame="3" data-i="choice" data-testid="helps-note" data-tone="accent" dir="ltr" role="button" tabindex="0" style=@3341312e2dcc>

"If your language does not use this passive form, you can state this in active form. Alternate translation: [the one that he entrusted to me] or [the one that he gave me the responsibility to preach]"
<div data-frame="3" data-i="choice" data-testid="helps-note" data-tone="accent" dir="ltr" role="button" tabindex="0" style=@3341312e2dcc>
" includes Paul, Titus, and all believers."
